messages.content: Now that the flights are set, I need the hotels for Washington February 9 through 11 and Boston February 11 through 13. Please compare the full cost, museum travel time, and cancellation terms before booking either one.
I’ll price two rooms in each city against the scheduled museum locations. Is this one room for one adult, and should I use the card ending in 1842 if you approve the reservations?

Yes, one adult in one room. You may use that card after I choose. The Washington review is at the National Portrait Gallery Tuesday morning, and the Boston receiving meeting is at the Museum of Fine Arts Friday at 8:00 a.m.

For Washington, the two strongest available options are Riggs Washington DC and Hotel Zena. Riggs is about 0.2 mile from the National Portrait Gallery, roughly a 4-minute walk. Its refundable king room is $259 per night for two nights, plus a $35 nightly destination fee and $93.79 in taxes, for $681.79 total. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. local time on February 7; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.
And Hotel Zena? I want the total calculated the same way.

Hotel Zena has a refundable king room at $229 per night. Two nights are $458, taxes are $73.05, and there is no destination fee, making the complete total $531.05. It is about 0.9 mile from the gallery: approximately an 18-minute walk or 8-12 minutes by car in normal morning traffic. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. local time on February 8; a later cancellation costs one night plus tax.
So Riggs costs $150.74 more, correct? Does its fee include anything I would actually need, and is either rate prepaid?

Correct. The difference is $150.74. The Riggs destination fee includes standard Wi-Fi, local calls, and a daily food-and-beverage credit, but none of those is required for the gallery visit. Both rates are pay-at-property and guaranteed by card rather than prepaid. Riggs is substantially closer, while Hotel Zena is less expensive and gives you one additional day to cancel.
Keep both open while we look at Boston. I need to know the practical trip to the MFA, not just straight-line distance.

The walkable Boston option is The Colonnade Hotel. A refundable king room is $279 nightly: $558 for two nights plus $91.79 in taxes, totaling $649.79, with no mandatory property fee. The MFA is about 0.8 mile away, normally a 16-18 minute walk along Huntington Avenue. A taxi is usually 5-9 minutes, depending on morning traffic. Free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. local time on February 8; after that, one night plus tax is charged.
What is the transit option, and exactly how much later can I cancel it?

Hyatt Regency Boston is the lower-cost transit option. Its refundable king room is $244 per night, or $488 for two nights, with $80.28 in taxes and no mandatory destination fee. The full total is $568.28. From the hotel, allow about 24-30 minutes: walk roughly 6 minutes to Boylston, take the Green Line toward Heath Street, exit at Museum of Fine Arts, then walk about 3 minutes. Free cancellation remains available until 11:59 p.m. local time on February 10, which is two days and nearly six hours later than The Colonnade’s deadline.
Is there any issue getting to the museum by 7:45 Friday from the Hyatt? I do not want the quoted time based on midday service.

For a 7:45 a.m. Friday arrival, current weekday schedules support leaving the Hyatt around 7:05. Trains are scheduled frequently at that hour, but I would allow 35-40 minutes door to door to cover the walk, waiting time, and minor delays. A taxi leaving around 7:15 would ordinarily take 12-20 minutes, though traffic can vary. The Colonnade is simpler because you could leave on foot around 7:25.
Please put all four choices into one concise comparison, including totals and deadlines.

Washington: Riggs, $681.79 total, 4-minute walk to the Portrait Gallery, cancel free through February 7 at 6:00 p.m.; Hotel Zena, $531.05 total, 18-minute walk or 8-12 minute drive, cancel free through February 8 at 6:00 p.m. Boston: The Colonnade, $649.79 total, 16-18 minute walk to the MFA, cancel free through February 8 at 6:00 p.m.; Hyatt Regency Boston, $568.28 total, allow 35-40 minutes by Green Line for the early meeting, cancel free through February 10 at 11:59 p.m. All deadlines are local hotel time, and every quoted room is refundable and paid at the property.

For Washington, take Riggs. The Tuesday review is the central commitment, and removing the morning car or long walk is worth the difference. For Boston, take the Hyatt; the later deadline matters because receiving details could still shift, and I can leave earlier.

Those selections total $1,250.07 across both stays. Before I submit them: Riggs Washington DC, king room, check-in February 9 and check-out February 11 for $681.79; Hyatt Regency Boston, king room, check-in February 11 and check-out February 13 for $568.28. Both are for Avery Thompson, one adult. May I guarantee both with the card ending in 1842 and accept the stated one-night cancellation penalties after their respective deadlines?
Yes. Use the card ending in 1842, accept those terms, and reserve both.

The Riggs reservation is confirmed. The guaranteed total is $681.79, payable at the hotel, including the two $35 destination fees and estimated taxes. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. Washington time on February 7; afterward, the penalty is one night plus tax. Confirmation: RIG-492731.
And Boston? Please verify that the late cancellation deadline remained attached to the room you actually booked.

The Hyatt Regency Boston reservation is also confirmed under the refundable king rate. The total is $568.28, payable at the hotel. I verified that free cancellation remains available through 11:59 p.m. Boston time on February 10; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. Confirmation: HYB-805416.
Good. Give me the final stay sequence with the museum access notes and the combined amount charged now.

February 9-11: Riggs Washington DC, confirmation RIG-492731, about a 4-minute walk to the National Portrait Gallery. February 11-13: Hyatt Regency Boston, confirmation HYB-805416; for the Friday 8:00 a.m. MFA meeting, plan to leave around 7:05 a.m. for the Green Line and allow 35-40 minutes. The combined guaranteed hotel total is $1,250.07. Nothing was charged now; both reservations are secured by the card ending in 1842 and are payable at the respective hotels, subject to their cancellation terms.
